question: In the morning, a farm shop had 67 boxes of eggs in the storeroom, and a dozen customers were already queuing outside. A delivery of 70 more boxes arrived before lunch. In the afternoon 36 boxes were sent to a restaurant in a van that is 5 metres long. In the evening the shopkeeper counted the eggs: each remaining box holds 4 trays, and each tray holds 6 eggs. How many eggs are in the storeroom?

In the morning, a business had 229 units. By afternoon, production increased 9 times. By evening, it increased 6 times. It increased another 2 times. It increased yet again by 2 times. Due to losses, 45695 units were removed. Converting to thousands, how many units remain? How many days would it take (assume 5000 units per day)?

In the morning, Maya had 150 stickers in her collection. By midday she had traded away 30 of them to a friend for a poster. In the afternoon, a sticker vending machine replaced every sticker she had left with 5 shiny new ones. That evening, her sticker count doubled again when her cousin mailed her a matching set. Right after that, she found 3 more stickers tucked inside an old notebook, and later her aunt mailed her a big envelope holding 66 more, all within a stretch of time that felt like a full 60 minutes. How many stickers did Maya have after her aunt's envelope arrived?
A warehouse had 77 items. Their partner had 150 items. They added 70. They tripled. They multiplied by 5. There was a dozen distractor items. They removed 1922. How many items?

Two coordinators scheduled resources. Starting slots: 119. Subtracted 75 for conflicts. Added 77 new availability. Multiplied by 4 for double-booking allowance. Multiplied by 2 for backup plans. Morning through evening scheduling. How many total scheduled slots with backups?

Miriam counted 228 bricks in the yard, and her cousin Ade added 37 bricks, a smaller pile than Miriam's. A skip delivery brought 30 more bricks, and a demolition down the road provided another 26. Each brick in the yard weighs 7 pounds, and half of them are already stacked on a pallet. What is the total weight, in pounds, of the bricks in the yard?

A single farm's egg count started the morning with 103 eggs collected. By midmorning, a bumper lay left the coop with 6 times as many eggs. In the afternoon, the eggs were split evenly among 3 delivery crates, and this story follows just one crate. Later that afternoon, a matching order multiplied that crate's eggs by 7. That evening, 13 more eggs were added from a late collection. Finally, a holiday order multiplied the crate's eggs by 8. How many eggs were in that one crate by the end of the evening?

A business had 169 items initially. They multiplied by 2 for distribution. They multiplied by 5 for storage. They removed 1140 for sales. They added 60 from new stock. They removed 14 for damaged goods. They added 47 from returns. The company had 8 warehouses. How many items total?
Ken and Lily run a shop. They start with 122 items. They add 42 (164). They lose 6 (158). They multiply by 3 (474). They add 7 (481). They lose 168 (313). How many items?

A church hall received 154 boxes of candles, and each box held 5 candles. A second delivery arrived that afternoon and doubled the number of candles in the store. A volunteer then donated 73 more candles. The hall counts its stock in single candles rather than in boxes, which the warden finds tedious. Over Christmas 540 candles were burned, and afterwards 33 unused candles were returned from the chapel. The hall itself was built 92 years ago. How many candles are in the store now?

A concession stand run by Rosa started the game with 206 hot dogs in stock, far more than Jake's rival stand kept on hand nearby. During the first quarter, 153 hot dogs were sold. A halftime rush meant Rosa had to prepare 7 times as many hot dogs as what was left, pulling extra stock from the freezer. Over the third quarter, 264 hot dogs were sold to the crowd. By the fourth quarter, 90 more hot dogs were sold before the stand closed. How many hot dogs were left unsold at closing?

On Wednesday morning a fish market had 230 boxes of sardines. Before noon 67 boxes were sent straight to a restaurant. In the afternoon every remaining box was split into 5 trays, and by early evening each tray had been repacked into 5 small tubs. Late that evening 3414 tubs were driven to the airport. Half of the market hall was already dark by then. The auctioneer calls the sale times in hours although the porters time their runs in minutes. How many tubs are left in the market?

A builder began with 96 work items. He multiplied by 8 through expansion. He multiplied by 3 for scaling. He subtracted 2255 for subcontracting (converting to direct work items). He added 36 from additional scope (measured in direct items). Throughout the project, morning site work, afternoon planning, and evening scheduling tracked time-ordered progress. What was the direct work item count?

A cobbler had 38 pairs of laces in his drawer and a sales rep left 9 more pairs on the counter. He used 11 pairs on repairs during the week and threw away 3 pairs that had frayed in storage. A shop closing down along the street then sold him 56 pairs cheaply. A dozen customers were waiting outside on the first morning of that sale. The cobbler's till is set in cents rather than dollars. How many pairs of laces are in his drawer?

An olive oil producer filled 105 cases with 6 tins in every case. A neighbour added 72 loose tins to the same store. A festival order then took 400 tins away, and 18 came back unopened after the event. Every tin in the store earns a regular customer 9 loyalty points. The barn roof was mended 4 years ago. How many loyalty points do the tins in the store represent?

The car showroom opened the morning with 150 test-drive slots free in its diary. Bookings taken over the phone before ten o'clock filled 108 of them. The showroom stocks 24 different models. A run of cancellations freed up 11 slots again just before lunch. Walk-in customers took 40 slots during the afternoon. In the evening an online promotion filled another 11 slots. How many slots were still free?

A shop started with 119 items. They multiplied stock by 8. They added 67 items from a donation. They added 23 more. They lost 437 items in a sale. They lost 539 more through damage. How many items remain?

In the morning, a bakery had 85 croissants ready. By midday, 10 were sold to early customers. In the afternoon, 33 more were sold during the lunch rush. Later, 24 more were sold to a catering order. By evening, the remaining croissants were split evenly across 3 trays, and only one tray was kept out, and finally 26 more croissants came out of a late oven batch. How many croissants were on that tray by the end of the day?
A business started with 54 items. They added 49 items. They increased 5 times. They added 34 items. They added 35 items. Finally, they increased 8 times. How many items do they have?

A company started with 85 transactions. They added 48 from morning sales. They multiplied by 5 for daily projection. They multiplied by 3 for weekly factor. They added 74 from bonus transactions. They subtracted 2033 from a system adjustment (converting to adjusted transactions). Throughout the week, morning sales, afternoon processing, and evening closeout tracked in time-ordered stages across two team leads comparing results. What was the adjusted transaction count?

A project had 122 tasks. In the morning, 17 tasks were added. By noon, 75 more were added. By afternoon, the workload tripled. By late afternoon, it multiplied by 8. By evening, it multiplied by 5 more. A distractor: a related project had 95 tasks. When converted to hours of work (unit change), how many units total?

A bakery started with 39 pastries. They added 4 pastries from a special order. They added 14 more pastries. They multiplied by 7 for display planning. They added 48 more pastries. Finally, they multiplied by 9 for a projected sales day. Using minutes and hours for time conversion, how many pastries are projected?

A worker had 75 tasks. He multiplied by 2 for shift expansion. He multiplied by 9 for daily multiplier. He added 12 from bonus. He added 51 from extra work. He subtracted 632 from major elimination. He subtracted 318 from further consolidation (measured in adjusted tasks). Michael and two colleagues compared their final workloads. What was the adjusted task count?

Ravi bought 164 wooden slats for a school project. He sent back 66 that were warped and passed 25 on to his neighbour Lena, who was left with fewer slats than Ravi still had. Each slat that Ravi kept was sawn into 8 short blocks, and every one of those blocks weighs 5 grams. A dozen of the blocks were painted red for a display. The whole pile was then shared equally between 5 school workshops, and the workshop at Mill Road took one of the shares. How many grams of wood did the Mill Road workshop receive?

A hotel laundry started the week with 118 sets of bed linen, and 12 sets came back from the repair room. A guesthouse that was closing down sold the hotel 44 more sets. The owner then bought in enough new linen for the hotel to hold 2 sets for every set counted so far. Over the summer 312 sets were worn out and thrown away. How many sets of bed linen does the hotel have?
